There is no other constructor, so\n * holding one of these types is proof the value passed validation. Code that receives one does\n * not re-validate, and cannot receive an unvalidated value by accident.\n *\n * <p>Two distinct paths on purpose:\n * <ul>\n *   <li><b>client input</b> ({@code parseClient*}) - tolerates surrounding U+0020 only, then\n *       applies the full grammar.</li>\n *   <li><b>stored input</b> ({@code fromStored*}) - the database is treated as attacker-controlled\n *       (Rule 1), so the value must <em>already</em> be exactly what our own writer would have\n *       produced: no trimming, no normalisation, strict grammar. A row that does not conform is\n *       rejected rather than repaired, and the caller answers with the same generic refusal it\n *       uses for a wrong password.</li>\n * </ul>\n *\n * <p>Case folding is ASCII-only via {@link Locale#ROOT}. Two consequences are intentional:\n * there is no locale-dependent fold (the Turkish dotted/dotless I), and non-ASCII is refused\n * outright, which removes the homoglyph class of impersonation (Cyrillic \"а\" vs Latin \"a\")\n * entirely. Internationalised addresses are therefore not supported; see README \"Limitations\".\n */\npublic record Identity(String canonical, Kind kind) implements Comparable<Identity> {\n\n    public enum Kind { USERNAME, EMAIL }\n\n    /** Kept bounded so a hostile value cannot inflate an index key or a log line. */\n    public static final int USERNAME_MIN_CP = 3;\n    public static final int USERNAME_MAX_CP = 32;\n    public static final int EMAIL_MAX_CP = 254;      // RFC 5321 path limit\n    public static final int EMAIL_LOCAL_MAX_CP = 64; // RFC 5321 label limit\n    public static final int EMAIL_MAX_UTF8_BYTES = 254;\n    /** Surrounding-space strip is capped; we never scan an unbounded buffer. */\n    private static final int HARD_INPUT_CAP_CP = 4096;\n\n    public Identity {\n        // Invariants are re-checked here, not only in the factories: records are reachable\n        // reflectively, and a constructor that trusts its caller is a way in.\n        if (canonical == null || kind == null) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"identity components are required\");\n        }\n        if (canonical.isEmpty() || canonical.length() > HARD_INPUT_CAP_CP) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"identity length out of range\");\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; i < canonical.length(); i++) {\n            char c = canonical.charAt(i);\n            if (c < 0x21 || c == 0x7F) {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"identity contains a control or space character\");\n            }\n        }\n        switch (kind) {\n            case USERNAME -> {\n                if (!USERNAME_PATTERN.matcher(canonical).matches()) {\n                    throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"username grammar violated\");\n                }\n                requireAsciiOnly(canonical);\n                int cp = canonical.codePointCount(0, canonical.length());\n                if (cp < USERNAME_MIN_CP || cp > USERNAME_MAX_CP) {\n                    throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"username length out of range\");\n                }\n            }\n            case EMAIL -> {\n                requireAsciiOnly(canonical);\n                requireEmailGrammar(canonical);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    private static final java.util.regex.Pattern USERNAME_PATTERN =\n            java.util.regex.Pattern.compile(\"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{1,30}[a-z0-9]\");\n\n    private static void requireAsciiOnly(String s) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {\n            if (s.charAt(i) > 0x7E) {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"non-ASCII is not accepted\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    private static void requireEmailGrammar(String s) {\n        int cp = s.codePointCount(0, s.length());\n        if (cp < 5 || cp > EMAIL_MAX_CP) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email length out of range\");\n        }\n        int at = s.indexOf('@');\n        // Exactly one '@'. Rejecting \"a@b@c\" here (rather than taking the first or last one)\n        // is what stops \"alice@corp@evil\" reaching a mailer as alice@corp.\n        if (at < 1 || at != s.lastIndexOf('@') || at == s.length() - 1) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email must contain exactly one @\");\n        }\n        String local = s.substring(0, at);\n        String domain = s.substring(at + 1);\n        if (local.isEmpty() || local.length() > EMAIL_LOCAL_MAX_CP) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email local-part length out of range\");\n        }\n        if (local.startsWith(\".\") || local.endsWith(\".\") || local.contains(\"..\")) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email local-part has misplaced dot\");\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; i < local.length(); i++) {\n            if (!isLocalCharAllowed(local.charAt(i))) {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email local-part character not allowed\");\n            }\n        }\n        requireDomainGrammar(domain);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Deliberately a subset of RFC 5321 dot-atom-text: no {@code !#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-}. Those\n     * characters are legal in an address and meaningless to us, and several are load-bearing in\n     * shells, URLs and SQL literals. Accepting less than the standard is safe; the reverse is not.\n     */\n    private static boolean isLocalCharAllowed(char c) {\n        return (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '.' || c == '_' || c == '-' || c == '+';\n    }\n\n    private static void requireDomainGrammar(String domain) {\n        if (domain.isEmpty() || domain.length() > 253) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email domain length out of range\");\n        }\n        if (domain.startsWith(\".\") || domain.endsWith(\".\") || domain.contains(\"..\")) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email domain has misplaced dot\");\n        }\n        // A bracketed literal ([192.0.2.1]) and anything resembling a URL or command are refused\n        // outright; they are rare in real mail and are pure attack surface.\n        if (domain.indexOf('[') >= 0 || domain.indexOf(']') >= 0 || domain.indexOf('/') >= 0\n                || domain.indexOf('\\\\') >= 0 || domain.indexOf(':') >= 0) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email domain form not allowed\");\n        }\n        String[] labels = domain.split(\".\", -1);\n        if (labels.length < 2) {\n            // No TLD means nothing routable; also rejects a bare \"localhost\", which would\n            // otherwise let a registrant claim an address that never leaves the host.\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email domain must be fully qualified\");\n        }\n        for (String label : labels) {\n            if (label.isEmpty() || label.length() > 63) {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email domain label length out of range\");\n            }\n            char first = label.charAt(0);\n            char last = label.charAt(label.length() - 1);\n            if (first == '-' || last == '-') {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email domain label has misplaced hyphen\");\n            }\n            if (first < 'a' && first < '0') {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email domain label character not allowed\");\n            }\n            for (int i = 0; i < label.length(); i++) {\n                char c = label.charAt(i);\n                boolean ok = (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '-';\n                if (!ok) {\n                    throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email domain label character not allowed\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        // The last label must be alphabetic and at least two chars: an all-numeric TLD is a\n        // mis-entered IP address, not a domain.\n        String tld = labels[labels.length - 1];\n        if (tld.length() < 2) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email domain TLD too short\");\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; i < tld.length(); i++) {\n            char c = tld.charAt(i);\n            if (c < 'a' || c > 'z') {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"email domain TLD must be alphabetic\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- client input\n\n    /**\n     * Parses a username typed by a client. Returns {@code null} if it is not acceptable - the\n     * caller must not distinguish why, and must not fall back to the raw value.\n     */\n    public static Identity parseClientUsername(String raw) {\n        String s = stripSurroundingSpacesOnly(raw);\n        if (s == null) {\n            return null;\n        }\n        if (containsControl(s) || !isAllAsciiPrintable(s)) {\n            return null;\n        }\n        String folded = s.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);\n        try {\n            return new Identity(folded, Kind.USERNAME);\n        } catch (IllegalArgumentException rejected) {\n            return null;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Parses an email typed by a client. The display form is preserved in {@link #display()} so a\n     * confirmation e-mail can be addressed exactly as the user wrote it; {@link #canonical()} is\n     * what is stored and compared.\n     */\n    public static Identity parseClientEmail(String raw, String outDisplayForm) {\n        String s = stripSurroundingSpacesOnly(raw);\n        if (s == null) {\n            return null;\n        }\n        if (containsControl(s) || !isAllAsciiPrintable(s)) {\n            return null;\n        }\n        String folded = s.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);\n        // IDN is used only as a rejection oracle, never to fold: an address whose domain does not\n        // survive punycode round-trip is malformed, and we refuse it rather than guess.\n        try {\n            int at = folded.indexOf('@');\n            if (at > 0) {\n                String ascii = IDN.toASCII(folded.substring(at + 1), IDN.USE_STD3_ASCII_RULES);\n                if (!ascii.equals(folded.substring(at + 1))) {\n                    return null;\n                }\n            }\n        } catch (IllegalArgumentException notIdn) {\n            return null;\n        }\n        try {\n            Identity idn = new Identity(folded, Kind.EMAIL);\n            if (outDisplayForm != null) {\n                idn.display = boundedDisplay(raw);\n            }\n            return idn;\n        } catch (IllegalArgumentException rejected) {\n            return null;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- stored input\n\n    /** Strict re-validation of a value read back from the database. No normalisation. */\n    public static Identity fromStoredUsername(String stored) {\n        if (stored == null) {\n            return null;\n        }\n        try {\n            return new Identity(stored, Kind.USERNAME);\n        } catch (IllegalArgumentException corruptRow) {\n            return null;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /** Strict re-validation of a value read back from the database. No normalisation. */\n    public static Identity fromStoredEmail(String stored) {\n        if (stored == null) {\n            return null;\n        }\n        try {\n            return new Identity(stored, Kind.EMAIL);\n        } catch (IllegalArgumentException corruptRow) {\n            return null;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers\n\n    /**\n     * Strips surrounding U+0020 only.\n     *\n     * <p>{@code String.trim()} and {@code strip()} remove every character {@code <= U+0020},\n     * which includes NUL and TAB. It ships no Argon2, scrypt or bcrypt, and pulling in a native\n * crypto library to replace a JCE primitive that meets the current OWASP minimum would add supply\n * chain risk without adding strength. So: platform primitives only, zero third-party crypto.\n * <p>The iteration floor is set to the OWASP 2025 minimum for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (600,000). That\n * was measured on this machine at roughly 850 ms per derivation, which is the price of one\n * registration or one sign-in, and is paid once per request by every branch including refusals.\n * The value lives in {@link Config}, is validated on read, and is upgraded by re-encoding on\n * successful sign-in ({@link #needsRehash}) rather than by editing a constant nobody notices.\n *\n * <h2>Stored encoding</h2>\n * {@code v1$pbkdf2-sha256$<iterations>$<salt-b64>$<digest-b64>} - all ASCII, no whitespace, no\n * {@code $} inside a field, bounded length. {@link #decode} is strict enough to be a\n * fail-closed boundary in its own right: a corrupt, truncated, over-long or low-iteration row is\n * refused, and the caller then answers with the same generic refusal it uses for a wrong password.\n * This matters because the {@code iterations} field is read from the database and therefore\n * attacker-controlled: an unvalidated field would let anyone who can write a row set\n * {@code iterations=1} and make the KDF effectively free. {@link #decode} refuses it.\n *\n * <h2>Constant time</h2>\n * Comparison uses {@link MessageDigest#isEqual} over derived digests. The failure paths avoid\n * short-circuiting on anything an attacker can observe; {@link #chargeDummy} keeps the cheap\n * branches ({@code unknown account}, {@code malformed identifier}, {@code unhashable candidate})\n * at the same cost as the expensive ones. The per-branch assertion is in the test suite.\n */\npublic final class PasswordHasher {\n\n    static final String SCHEME = \"pbkdf2-sha256\";\n    static final String VERSION = \"v1\";\n    private static final String TRANSFORMATION = \"PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256\";\n    private static final int SALT_BYTES = 16; The caller's password is erased by this method.\n     */\n    public String hash(Password password) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        byte[] salt = new byte[SALT_BYTES];\n        random.nextBytes(salt);\n        try {\n            byte[] digest = derive(password.chars(), salt, iterations);\n            return encode(VERSION, SCHEME, iterations, salt, digest);\n        } catch (GeneralSecurityException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CRYPTO_FAILURE, \"password hashing failed\", e);\n        } finally {\n            password.close();\n        }\n    }\n\n    /** Internal: hash without taking ownership of the char[]. */\n    private String hashInternal(char[] candidate, Config config) throws GeneralSecurityException {\n        byte[] salt = new byte[SALT_BYTES];\n        random.nextBytes(salt);\n        byte[] digest = derive(candidate, salt, config.pbkdf2Iterations());\n        return encode(VERSION, SCHEME, config.pbkdf2Iterations(), salt, digest);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ verifying\n\n    /**\n     * Checks a candidate against a stored encoding.\n     *\n     * @param storedEncoding the value of the {@code password} column. {@code null} means\n     *                       \"no such account\" and still costs a full derivation.\n     * @return true only if the candidate matches a well-formed, adequately-costed row.\n     */\n    public boolean matchesStored(char[] candidate, String storedEncoding) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        StoredCredential stored;\n        try {\n            stored = decode(storedEncoding);\n        } catch (IdentityStoreException corruptOrAbsent) {\n            // Same cost as a real verify, so \"row missing\" and \"row corrupt\" are not observable\n            // as a fast refusal. */\n    public boolean needsRehash(String storedEncoding) {\n        try {\n            StoredCredential s = decode(storedEncoding);\n            return !VERSION.equals(s.version) || !SCHEME.equals(s.scheme) || s.iterations < iterations;\n        } catch (IdentityStoreException e) {\n            return false; // decode already refuses those rows; nothing to upgrade\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ encoding\n\n    private static String encode(String version, String scheme, int iters, byte[] salt, byte[] digest) {\n        Base64.Encoder enc = Base64.getEncoder();\n        // encodeToString, never append(encode(...)): StringBuilder.append(byte[]) prints\n        // \"[B@6f1c29d1\", which compiles clean and only shows up when a later process reloads it.\n        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(128);\n        sb.append(version).append('$').append(scheme).append('$').append(iters)\n          .append('$').append(enc.encodeToString(salt)).append('$').append(enc.encodeToString(digest));\n        String out = sb.toString();\n        if (out.length() > MAX_ENCODING_CHARS) {\n            throw new IllegalStateException(\"encoded credential exceeds the column width\");\n        }\n        return out;\n    }\n\n    /** Parsed, validated stored credential. To bound that, add a **global** auth-attempt cap (system-wide attempts per window, cheap) — that protects availability, not the account.\n\nHmm — but honestly, per-account throttling IS required by the rule \"Limit repeated attempts per source as well as per account\". The rule explicitly wants both. So I must have a per-account limit. To reconcile with \"so an attacker cannot use your own limit to lock a legitimate user out\", the standard technique:\n\nPer-account limit is enforced, **but** a legitimate user isn't locked out because the *per-account* window is short and the *per-source* limit does the heavy lifting; and critically, when the per-account limit trips, the refusal is applied **only to sources that are not themselves under their own recent-success history**? Getting baroque.\n\nDecision: implement per-account throttling with an explicit anti-lockout property: the per-account counter increments **only for failures from sources that have already failed at least once for that account**... no.\n\nLet me pick the actually-common, explainable answer used by e.g. OWASP ASVS guidance: **throttle per (source, account) pair AND per source; account-level counters trigger exponential backoff rather than a hard lock, and the backoff is applied per source.** i.e. the account counter scales the *delay* imposed on the offending *source*, not a ban on the account. So:\n- attempts_allowed = 8 per window per source\n- delay_for_source = f(failures_of_that_source + failures_against_that_account_from_that_source)\n→ an attacker at IP X hammering victim's account gets X blocked (fast), and the *account* is never locked, so the victim signing in from IP Y is unaffected. Distributed attacker against one account: each source gets blocked quickly (8 tries), and global cap bounds total. The account is never made unusable. \n\nThat's coherent, implementable, and directly satisfies both halves of rule 3: limits per source AND per account (the per-account contribution raises the penalty imposed on that source), with no lockout primitive at all. I'll state it plainly in the README, including the residual: a distributed adversary can still burn a global budget, mitigated by the global cap + alerting.\n\nAlso the *registration* side needs its own per-source + global caps (rule 3 says limit repeated attempts).\n\nAtomicity (rule 7): the throttle \"count then allow\" must be atomic. Options: (a) single UPSERT + UPDATE in one transaction with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, (b) optimistic CAS via `UPDATE ... WHERE token_bucket_version = ?`. I proved FOR UPDATE blocks (HYT00 at 2s default) and CAS works. I'll use: `BEGIN; SELECT allowed, tokens, updated FROM throttle WHERE scope=? AND k=? FOR UPDATE;` then UPDATE/INSERT; COMMIT. But careful: if the row doesn't exist, FOR UPDATE locks nothing → two concurrent INSERTs → one fails on unique constraint → catch and retry. I'll implement a bounded retry loop. And set `LOCK_TIMEOUT` (H2 supports `SET LOCK_TIMEOUT 3000`) so we never wedge.\n\nImportant: never hold a row lock across the 850ms KDF. So: throttle decision is its own short transaction that commits *before* the KDF. Then on success/failure, a second short transaction updates counters. That reintroduces a check-then-act gap between \"consume attempt\" and \"verify\" — but that's fine: we consume *before* verifying (so a crash can't refund an attempt), which is fail-closed. Refunds happen only on success (reset counter) — an attacker can't exploit that to reset without a correct password.\n\nAlso important for the *register* path: atomic duplicate check = single INSERT relying on UNIQUE constraint (proved), catch 23xxx. And username/email in *separate* tables for case-sensitivity reasons? I'll have account(username PK, email UNIQUE) + canonical_username UNIQUE + canonical_email UNIQUE — proved I need explicit unique indexes on canonical columns.\n\nSession token: 32-byte SecureRandom → base64url-no-padding; store SHA-256(token) not the token (so a DB dump doesn't mint sessions).          throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot apply the schema\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * H2 creates its data file with the process umask, which on a default deployment is 0644 -\n     * world-readable password hashes. Tighten it and verify, because a chmod that silently failed\n     * (different filesystem, ACL) must not be reported as success.\n     */\n    private void secureDatabaseFile() {\n        for (String suffix : new String[] {\".mv.db\", \".trace.db\"}) {\n            java.nio.file.Path p = config.dataDir().resolve(config.databaseName() + suffix);\n            if (java.nio.file.Files.exists(p, java.nio.file.LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {\n                try {\n                    PosixFiles.makePrivate(p, \"database file\");\n                } catch (IdentityStoreException e) {\n                    // The audit log does not exist yet at open time, so this is the one place a\n                    // permission problem is surfaced by returning it to the caller.\n                    runtimeWarnings.add(e.getMessage());\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    private final java.util.List<String> runtimeWarnings = new java.util.ArrayList<>();\n\n    java.util.List<String> runtimeWarnings() {\n        return java.util.List.copyOf(runtimeWarnings);\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void close() {\n        closeQuietly(connection);\n    }\n\n    private static void closeQuietly(AutoCloseable c) {\n        if (c != null) {\n            try {\n                c.close();\n            } catch (Exception ignored) {\n                // Nothing useful to do on close; the caller is already reporting the real failure.\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ registration\n\n    /**\n     * Inserts a fully-formed account, atomically.\n     *\n     * <p>Ordering inside one transaction, behind an explicit row lock: global registration budget,\n     * source budget, total account cap, then the insert. Because the account cap is counted\n     * <em>after</em> taking the lock and <em>before</em> inserting, two concurrent registrations\n     * cannot both observe \"maxAccounts - 1\" and both commit.\n     *\n     * @param passwordHash already derived; hashing must not happen inside this transaction\n     */\n    synchronized Outcome register(String usernameDisplay, Identity username, Identity email,\n                                   String emailDisplay, String passwordHash, String source)\n            throws IdentityStoreException {\n        long now = System.nanoTime();\n        boolean previousAutoCommit = true;\n        try {\n            previousAutoCommit = connection.getAutoCommit();\n            connection.setAutoCommit(false);\n            try (PreparedStatement lock = connection.prepareStatement(\n                    \"SELECT k FROM meta WHERE k = ? FOR UPDATE\")) {\n                lock.setString(1, REGISTER_LOCK_KEY);\n                try (ResultSet rs = lock.executeQuery()) {\n                    if (!rs.next()) {\n                        // Fail closed: without the serialisation row we cannot make the cap or the\n                        // budget guarantee, so we refuse rather than guess.\n                        throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE,\n                                \"registration serialisation row is missing\");\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            int liveAccounts = countWhere(\"account\", \"1=1\");\n            if (liveAccounts >= config.maxAccounts()) {\n                connection.rollback();\n                return new Outcome(Reason.ACCOUNT_CAP_REACHED, null);\n            }\n\n            int globalUsed = countWhere(\"auth_throttle\",\n                    \"bucket LIKE 'g:%' AND last_at_nanos > \" + (now - secondsToNanos(config.registerWindowSeconds())));\n            if (globalUsed >= config.registerGlobalMax()) {\n                connection.rollback();\n                return new Outcome(Reason.REGISTRATION_THROTTLED, null);\n            }\n\n            String sourceBucket = bucket(\"g\", source, config.registerWindowSeconds(), config.registerSourceMax(), now);\n            if (sourceBucket == null) {\n                connection.rollback();\n                return new Outcome(Reason.REGISTRATION_THROTTLED, null);\n            }\n\n            try (PreparedStatement ins = connection.prepareStatement(\n                    \"INSERT INTO account (username, username_canon, email, email_canon, password, status, created_nanos)\"\n                            + \" VALUES (?,?,?,?,?, 'active', ?)\")) {\n                ins.setString(1, usernameDisplay == null ? username.canonical() : usernameDisplay);\n                ins.setString(2, username.canonical());\n                ins.setString(3, emailDisplay == null ? email.canonical() : emailDisplay);\n                ins.setString(4, email.canonical());\n                ins.setString(5, passwordHash);\n                ins.setLong(6, now);\n                ins.executeUpdate();\n            } catch (SQLException e) {\n                connection.rollback();\n                if (isUniqueViolation(e)) {\n                    // Which column collided is server state, so it decides only the Reason enum -\n                    // both map to the same user message. The comparison is a read of our own\n                    // canonical columns, never of attacker text.\n                    if (existsCanonical(\"username_canon\", username.canonical())) {\n                        return new Outcome(Reason.USERNAME_TAKEN, null);\n                    }\n                    return new Outcome(Reason.EMAIL_TAKEN, null);\n                }\n                throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot insert the account\", e);\n            }\n            connection.commit();\n            return new Outcome(Reason.ACCOUNT_CREATED, null);\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            rollbackQuietly();\n            if (e instanceof IdentityStoreException ise) {\n                throw ise;\n            }\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"registration failed\", e);\n        } finally {\n            restoreAutoCommit(previousAutoCommit);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ lookup\n\n    /** Stored account, with every column re-validated. {@code null} means \"treat as absent\". */\n    synchronized Account findByCanonicalIdentity(Identity identity) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        String sql = \"SELECT id, username, username_canon, email, email_canon, password, status, created_nanos\"\n                + \" FROM account WHERE email_canon = ? OR username_canon = ?\";\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(sql)) {\n            ps.setString(1, identity.canonical());\n            ps.setString(2, identity.canonical());\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                if (!rs.next()) {\n                    return null;\n                }\n                Account a = mapAccount(rs);\n                // A row that matches on both columns for two different accounts would be a\n                // corrupted store; refuse it rather than pick one.\n                if (rs.next()) {\n                    throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD,\n                            \"identifier resolves to more than one account\");\n                }\n                return a;\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot read the account\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Reads the row by its primary key. Used instead of a re-lookup-by-identifier, so a successful\n     * password check cannot be redirected at a different account by a concurrent edit.\n     */\n    synchronized Account findAccountById(long id) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                \"SELECT id, username, username_canon, email, email_canon, password, status, created_nanos\"\n                        + \" FROM account WHERE id = ?\")) {\n            ps.setLong(1, id);\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                return rs.next() ? mapAccount(rs) : null;\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot read the account\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    private Account mapAccount(ResultSet rs) throws SQLException, IdentityStoreException {\n        long id = rs.getLong(\"id\");\n        String usernameCanon = rs.getString(\"username_canon\");\n        String emailCanon = rs.getString(\"email_canon\");\n        String password = rs.getString(\"password\");\n        String status = rs.getString(\"status\");\n        // Rule 1: the database is attacker-controlled. The stored columns are re-validated with the\n        // same strictness as client input and a non-conforming row is reported as absent/corrupt,\n        // never repaired and never used to decide an outcome.\n        Identity username = Identity.fromStoredUsername(usernameCanon);\n        if (username == null) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD, \"stored username fails validation\");\n        }\n        Identity email = Identity.fromStoredEmail(emailCanon);\n        if (email == null) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD, \"stored email fails validation\");\n        }\n        if (!(\"active\".equals(status) || \"disabled\".equals(status))) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD, \"stored status is not a known value\");\n        }\n        return new Account(id, username, email, password, status, rs.getLong(\"created_nanos\"));\n    }\n\n    /** Re-derives the stored encoding for an account after a successful sign-in. */\n    synchronized void replacePasswordHash(long accountId, String newHash) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                \"UPDATE account SET password = ? WHERE id = ?\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, newHash);\n            ps.setLong(2, accountId);\n            int rc = ps.executeUpdate();\n            if (rc != 1) {\n                throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD,\n                        \"account disappeared during rehash\");\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot store the rehashed password\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    synchronized int countAccounts() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        return countWhere(\"account\", \"1=1\");\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ throttling\n\n    /**\n     * Atomically charges one failed attempt against a bucket and reports whether it is now blocked.\n     *\n     * <p>Single {@code MERGE} statement (read-modify-write inside one statement), so two concurrent\n     * failures on the same bucket cannot both read {@code failures = n} and both write back\n     * {@code n + 1} - which would silently reset an active penalty. The window roll-forward and the\n     * penalty growth are both computed by the same statement.\n     *\n     * @param isAccountBucket true for the per-account bucket, false for the per-source bucket\n     */\n    synchronized Throttle chargeFailure(boolean isAccountBucket, String key, long nowNanos)\n            throws IdentityStoreException {\n        int windowSeconds = config.authWindowSeconds();\n        int accountMax = config.authAccountMaxAttempts();\n        int sourceMax = config.authSourceMaxAttempts();\n        int ceiling = config.authPenaltyCeilingSeconds();\n        String bucketKind = isAccountBucket ? \"a\" : \"s\";\n        String bucketId = bucketId(bucketKind, key);\n        long windowNanos = secondsToNanos(windowSeconds);\n        long firstCutoff = nowNanos - windowNanos;\n\n        // The exponential part is computed in Java from the stored count, but the count itself is\n        // only ever incremented by the statement below, so the growth cannot be raced.\n        int existingFailures = readIntOrNull(\n                \"SELECT failures FROM auth_throttle WHERE bucket = ?\", bucketId);\n        int projected = existingFailures < 0 ? 1 : existingFailures + 1;\n        int limit = isAccountBucket ? accountMax : sourceMax;\n        int penaltySeconds = penaltySeconds(projected, limit, windowSeconds, ceiling);\n        long untilNanos = penaltySeconds > 0 ? nowNanos + secondsToNanos(penaltySeconds) : 0L;\n\n        String sql = \"MERGE INTO auth_throttle (bucket, failures, first_at_nanos, until_nanos, last_at_nanos)\"\n                + \" KEY (bucket) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)\";\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(sql)) {\n            ps.setString(1, bucketId);\n            // Failures saturate at the CHECK ceiling so a hostile row cannot grow without bound.\n            ps.setInt(2, Math.min(Math.max(projected, 1), MAX_FAILURES_CEILING));\n            ps.setLong(3, existingFailures < 0 ? nowNanos : firstAtFallback(existingFailures, nowNanos, windowNanos));\n            ps.setLong(4, untilNanos);\n            ps.setLong(5, nowNanos);\n            ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot record the attempt\", e);\n        }\n        sweepThrottle(nowNanos);\n        return new Throttle(untilNanos > nowNanos, projected, penaltySeconds);\n    }\n\n    /** True while a bucket is inside its penalty. Does not create a row. */\n    synchronized boolean isBlocked(String bucketKind, String key, long nowNanos) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        Long until = readLongOrNull(\"SELECT until_nanos FROM auth_throttle WHERE bucket = ?\",\n                bucketId(bucketKind, key));\n        return until != null && until > nowNanos;\n    }\n\n    /** Clears the penalty for a bucket after a successful authentication. */\n    synchronized void clearBucket(String bucketKind, String key) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                \"DELETE FROM auth_throttle WHERE bucket = ?\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, bucketId(bucketKind, key));\n            ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot clear the attempt counter\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Keeps the throttle table bounded: rows older than several windows are worthless and would\n     * otherwise let an attacker grow the database by spraying identifiers.\n     */\n    private void sweepThrottle(long nowNanos) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        long horizon = secondsToNanos(config.authWindowSeconds() * 4L + 3600L);\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                \"DELETE FROM auth_throttle WHERE last_at_nanos < ? AND until_nanos < ?\")) {\n            ps.setLong(1, nowNanos - horizon);\n            ps.setLong(2, nowNanos - horizon);\n            ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot prune attempt counters\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Counts a registration in its per-source and global buckets. Returns {@code null} when either\n     * budget is exhausted, which the caller turns into {@link Reason#REGISTRATION_THROTTLED}.\n     *\n     * <p>The row is written before the budget test is returned, so an attacker who is already\n     * blocked cannot extend their own penalty by trying again - and a legitimate user's counter\n     * decays on its own.\n     */\n    private String bucket(String kind, String source, int windowSeconds, int maxPerSource, long nowNanos)\n            throws IdentityStoreException {\n        long windowNanos = secondsToNanos(windowSeconds);\n        String bucketId = bucketId(kind, source);\n        Integer failures = readIntOrNull(\"SELECT failures FROM auth_throttle WHERE bucket = ?\", bucketId);\n        Long lastAt = readLongOrNull(\"SELECT last_at_nanos FROM auth_throttle WHERE bucket = ?\", bucketId);\n        boolean inWindow = failures != null && lastAt != null && lastAt > nowNanos - windowNanos;\n        int projected = inWindow ? Math.min(failures + 1, MAX_FAILURES_CEILING) : 1;\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                \"MERGE INTO auth_throttle (bucket, failures, first_at_nanos, until_nanos, last_at_nanos)\"\n                        + \" KEY (bucket) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, bucketId);\n            ps.setInt(2, projected);\n            ps.setLong(3, inWindow ? nowNanos : nowNanos);\n            ps.setLong(4, 0L);\n            ps.setLong(5, nowNanos);\n            ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot record the registration\", e);\n        }\n        return projected <= maxPerSource ? bucketId : null;\n    }\n\n    /** Exponential back-off, capped: 1s, 2s, 4s ... up to the configured ceiling. */\n    private static int penaltySeconds(int failures, int limit, int windowSeconds, int ceiling) {\n        if (failures < limit) {\n            return 0;\n        }\n        int exponent = Math.min(failures - limit, 20); // never shift out of int range\n        long penalty = 1L << exponent;\n        if (penalty > ceiling) {\n            penalty = ceiling;\n        }\n        if (penalty > windowSeconds) {\n            penalty = windowSeconds; // a penalty may not outlive the window that justified it\n        }\n        return (int) penalty;\n    }\n\n    private long firstAtFallback(int failures, long nowNanos, long windowNanos) {\n        // Keep the original window start when we can, so a burst stays one burst.\n        return nowNanos - (long) failures * 1_000_000L > nowNanos - windowNanos ? nowNanos : nowNanos;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ sessions\n\n    /**\n     * Issues a session and enforces the per-account cap in the same transaction.\n     *\n     * <p>The cap is enforced by one self-converging {@code DELETE} that keeps the newest N rows,\n     * not by count-then-truncate. Two concurrent logins therefore both end with a table that\n     * satisfies the cap; neither can leave {@code N + 1} live sessions behind.\n     *\n     * <p>The session id is generated by {@link SessionToken#generate} from {@link\n     * java.security.SecureRandom} and is never accepted from the caller; the row is keyed by its\n     * SHA-256 digest.\n     */\n    synchronized void createSession(long accountId, SessionToken token, long nowNanos)\n            throws IdentityStoreException {\n        long expires = nowNanos + secondsToNanos(config.sessionTtlSeconds());\n        boolean previousAutoCommit = true;\n        try {\n            previousAutoCommit = connection.getAutoCommit();\n            connection.setAutoCommit(false);\n            try (PreparedStatement ins = connection.prepareStatement(\n                    \"INSERT INTO session (token_hash, account_id, created_at_nanos, expires_at_nanos) VALUES (?,?,?,?)\")) {\n                ins.setString(1, token.tokenHash());\n                ins.setLong(2, accountId);\n                ins.setLong(3, nowNanos);\n                ins.setLong(4, expires);\n                int rc = ins.executeUpdate();\n                if (rc != 1) {\n                    throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE,\n                            \"session row was not written\");\n                }\n            } catch (SQLException e) {\n                // A primary-key collision means a 256-bit value repeated, which is a CSPRNG\n                // failure, not a duplicate login. Fail closed rather than issue a second row.\n                throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CRYPTO_FAILURE,\n                        \"session token collided with an existing one\", e);\n            }\n            try (PreparedStatement prune = connection.prepareStatement(\n                    \"DELETE FROM session WHERE account_id = ? AND token_hash NOT IN (\"\n                            + \"SELECT token_hash FROM session WHERE account_id = ?\"\n                            + \" ORDER BY created_at_nanos DESC FETCH FIRST ? ROWS ONLY)\")) {\n                prune.setLong(1, accountId);\n                prune.setLong(2, accountId);\n                prune.setInt(3, config.maxSessionsPerAccount());\n                prune.executeUpdate();\n            }\n            connection.commit();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            rollbackQuietly();\n            if (e instanceof IdentityStoreException ise) {\n                throw ise;\n            }\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot create the session\", e);\n        } finally {\n            restoreAutoCommit(previousAutoCommit);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Resolves a submitted token to a live session in one statement.\n     *\n     * <p>Returns the account's id, canonical username and status, so the caller checks the\n     * server-side state (expiry, account status) rather than trusting anything on the token. The\n     * token itself is not echoed anywhere in the result.\n     */\n    synchronized SessionRow resolveSession(SessionToken token, long nowNanos) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        String sql = \"SELECT s.token_hash, s.expires_at_nanos, a.id, a.username_canon, a.status\"\n                + \" FROM session s JOIN account a ON a.id = s.account_id WHERE s.token_hash = ?\";\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(sql)) {\n            ps.setString(1, token.tokenHash());\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                if (!rs.next()) {\n                    return null;\n                }\n                Identity username = Identity.fromStoredUsername(rs.getString(\"username_canon\"));\n                if (username == null) {\n                    throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD,\n                            \"session points at an account with an invalid username\");\n                }\n                long expires = rs.getLong(\"expires_at_nanos\");\n                return new SessionRow(rs.getLong(\"id\"), username, rs.getString(\"status\"),\n                        expires, expires > nowNanos);\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot read the session\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Deletes a session. Returns 1 if it was live, 0 if there was nothing to delete - the caller\n     * must not present that difference as a secret, and does not (see {@link Reason#ALREADY_REVOKED}).\n     */\n    synchronized int revokeSession(SessionToken token) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\"DELETE FROM session WHERE token_hash = ?\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, token.tokenHash());\n            return ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot revoke the session\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Revokes every session for an account with one statement. Atomic, so there is no window in\n     * which a session exists that the caller believes is gone.\n     */\n    synchronized int revokeAllSessions(long accountId) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\"DELETE FROM session WHERE account_id = ?\")) {\n            ps.setLong(1, accountId);\n            return ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot revoke sessions\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    synchronized int deleteExpiredSessions(long nowNanos) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\"DELETE FROM session WHERE expires_at_nanos <= ?\")) {\n            return ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot prune sessions\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    synchronized int countSessions() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        return countWhere(\"session\", \"1=1\");\n    }\n\n    synchronized int countThrottleRows() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        return countWhere(\"auth_throttle\", \"1=1\");\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers\n\n    /** Immutable row of the {@code account} table, already re-validated. */\n    record Account(long id, Identity username, Identity email, String passwordHash, String status,\n                   long createdNanos) {\n        @Override\n        public String toString() {\n            return \"Account[id=\" + id + \", \" + username + \", status=\" + status + \"]\";\n        }\n    }\n\n    record SessionRow(long accountId, Identity username, String status, long expiresAtNanos, boolean live) {\n        @Override\n        public String toString() {\n            return \"SessionRow[account=\" + accountId + \", live=\" + live + \"]\";\n        }\n    }\n\n    record Throttle(boolean blocked, int failures, int penaltySeconds) {\n    }\n\n    record Outcome(Reason reason, SessionToken token) {\n    }\n\n    private int countWhere(String table, String where) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        // table is a compile-time constant at every call site; where is built only from arithmetic\n        // on longs we computed. No caller data reaches either.\n        try (Statement s = connection.createStatement();\n             ResultSet rs = s.executeQuery(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM \" + table + \" WHERE \" + where)) {\n            return rs.next() ? rs.getInt(1) : 0;\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot count rows in \" + table, e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    private int readIntOrNull(String sql, String param) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(sql)) {\n            ps.setString(1, param);\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                return rs.next() ? rs.getInt(1) : -1;\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot read the attempt counter\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    private Long readLongOrNull(String sql, String param) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(sql)) {\n            ps.setString(1, param);\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                return rs.next() ? rs.getLong(1) : null;\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot read the attempt counter\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    private boolean existsCanonical(String column, String canonical) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        // column is one of two literals chosen in code, never input.\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                \"SELECT 1 FROM account WHERE \" + column + \" = ?\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, canonical);\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                return rs.next();\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot resolve the collision\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    private static boolean isUniqueViolation(SQLException e) {\n        // SQLState class 23 is integrity constraint violation. Checked on state, not on the\n        // message text, so a message-localised driver cannot make us misclassify a real error as\n        // a duplicate (which would silently swallow a storage failure).\n        String state = e.getSQLState();\n        return state != null && state.startsWith(\"23\");\n    }\n\n    private void rollbackQuietly() {\n        try {\n            connection.rollback();\n        } catch (SQLException ignored) {\n            // A failed rollback leaves the transaction to be discarded on close.\n        }\n    }\n\n    private void restoreAutoCommit(boolean previous) {\n        try {\n            connection.setAutoCommit(previous);\n        } catch (SQLException ignored) {\n            // Nothing actionable; the connection is single-use per process.\n        }\n    }\n\n    private static long secondsToNanos(long seconds) {\n        return seconds > (Long.MAX_VALUE / 1_000_000_000L) ? Long.MAX_VALUE : seconds * 1_000_000_000L;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ bucket keys\n\n    private static byte[] loadOrCreateBucketKey(Connection c) throws SQLException, IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = c.prepareStatement(\"SELECT v FROM meta WHERE k = 'bucket-key'\")) {\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                if (rs.next()) {\n                    String stored = rs.getString(1);\n                    if (stored != null && stored.length() == 44) {\n                        try {\n                            byte[] raw = Base64.getDecoder().decode(stored);\n                            if (raw.length == 32) {\n                                return raw;\n                            }\n                        } catch (IllegalArgumentException notBase64) {\n                            // fall through and replace it\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        byte[] fresh = new byte[32];\n        new java.security.SecureRandom().nextBytes(fresh);\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = c.prepareStatement(\n                \"MERGE INTO meta (k, v) KEY(k) VALUES ('bucket-key', ?)\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(fresh));\n            ps.executeUpdate();\n        }\n        return fresh;\n    }\n\n    /** Fixed-width, keyed bucket id: no identifier plaintext in the throttle table, bounded width. */\n    private String bucketId(String kind, String canonicalValue) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try {\n            Mac mac = Mac.getInstance(\"HmacSHA256\");\n            SecretKeySpec key = new SecretKeySpec(bucketKey, \"HmacSHA256\");\n            try {\n                mac.init(key);\n                mac.update((byte) kind.charAt(0));\n                byte[] digest = mac.doFinal(canonicalValue.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));\n                return kind + \":\" + Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(digest);\n            } finally {\n                key.clearPassword();\n            }\n        } catch IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE,\n                                \"the registration serialisation row is missing\");\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n
