return new Outcome(Reason.ACCOUNT_CAP_REACHED, null);\n                }\n\n                Budget global = readBudget(BUCKET_ID_GLOBAL_REGISTER, now,\n                        config.registerWindowSeconds(), config.registerGlobalMax());\n                if (global.exhausted()) {\n                    connection.rollback();\n                    return new Outcome(Reason.REGISTRATION_THROTTLED, null);\n                }\n\n                String sourceBucket = bucketId(BUCKET_KIND_SOURCE, email.canonical() + \"|\" + username.canonical());\n                Budget perSource = readBudget(sourceBucket, now,\n                        config.registerWindowSeconds(), config.registerSourceMax());\n                if (perSource.exhausted()) {\n                    connection.rollback();\n                    return new Outcome(Reason.REGISTRATION_THROTTLED, null);\n                }\n\n                try (PreparedStatement ins = connection.prepareStatement(\n                        \"INSERT INTO account (username, username_canon, email, email_canon, password, status,\"\n                                + \" created_epoch_s) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?, 'active', ?)\")) {\n                    ins.setString(1, usernameDisplay);\n                    ins.setString(2, username.canonical());\n                    ins.setString(3, emailDisplay);\n                    ins.setString(4, email.canonical());\n                    ins.setString(5, passwordHash);\n                    ins.setLong(6, now);\n                    ins.executeUpdate();\n                } catch (SQLException e) {\n                    connection.rollback();\n                    if (isUniqueViolation(e)) {\n                        // Which column collided is server state, and it selects only the Reason\n                        // enum - both map to the same user-visible message. The probe reads our own\n                        // canonical column, never attacker text.\n                        if (existsCanonical(\"username_canon\", username.canonical())) {\n                            return new Outcome(Reason.USERNAME_TAKEN, null);\n                        }\n                        return new Outcome(Reason.EMAIL_TAKEN, null);\n                    }\n                    throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot insert the account\", e);\n                }\n\n                // Success: charge both budgets, then commit, all under the same row lock.\n                chargeBudget(BUCKET_ID_GLOBAL_REGISTER, now, config.registerWindowSeconds());\n                chargeBudget(sourceBucket, now, config.registerWindowSeconds());\n                connection.commit();\n                return new Outcome(Reason.ACCOUNT_CREATED, null);\n            } catch (SQLException | IdentityStoreException e) {\n                connection.rollback();\n                if (e instanceof IdentityStoreException ise) {\n                    throw ise;\n                }\n                throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"registration failed\", e);\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            rollbackQuietly();\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"registration failed\", e);\n        } finally {\n            restoreAutoCommit(previousAutoCommit);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ lookup\n\n    /**\n     * Finds an account by either canonical form. Returns {@code null} for \"no such account\" and\n     * throws {@link Reason#CORRUPT_RECORD} for a row that fails strict re-validation - the caller\n     * treats both identically.\n     */\n    synchronized Account findByCanonicalIdentity(Identity identity) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        String sql = \"SELECT id, username, username_canon, email, email_canon, password, status, created_epoch_s\"\n                + \" FROM account WHERE email_canon = ? OR username_canon = ?\";\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(sql)) {\n            ps.setString(1, identity.canonical());\n            ps.setString(2, identity.canonical());\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                if (!rs.next()) {\n                    return null;\n                }\n                Account a = mapAccount(rs);\n                if (rs.next()) {\n                    // Two rows reachable by one identifier is a corrupted store; refuse rather than\n                    // pick whichever the engine happened to return first.\n                    throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD,\n                            \"the identifier resolves to more than one account\");\n                }\n                return a;\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot read the account\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Re-reads by primary key after a successful password check, so the outcome is bound to the row\n     * we verified rather than to a second identifier lookup that a concurrent edit could redirect.\n     */\n    synchronized Account findAccountById(long id) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                \"SELECT id, username, username_canon, email, email_canon, password, status, created_epoch_s\"\n                        + \" FROM account WHERE id = ?\")) {\n            ps.setLong(1, id);\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                return rs.next() ? mapAccount(rs) : null;\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot read the account\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    private Account mapAccount(ResultSet rs) throws SQLException, IdentityStoreException {\n        long id = rs.getLong(\"id\");\n        String password = rs.getString(\"password\");\n        String status = rs.getString(\"status\");\n        // Rule 1: the database is attacker-controlled. Both canonical columns are re-validated with\n        // the same strictness as client input; a non-conforming row is reported corrupt, never\n        // repaired and never allowed to decide an outcome.\n        Identity username = Identity.fromStoredUsername(rs.getString(\"username_canon\"));\n        if (username == null) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD, \"the stored username fails validation\");\n        }\n        Identity email = Identity.fromStoredEmail(rs.getString(\"email_canon\"));\n        if (email == null) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD, \"the stored email fails validation\");\n        }\n        if (!\"active\".equals(status) && !\"disabled\".equals(status)) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD, \"the stored status is not a known value\");\n        }\n        return new Account(id, username, email, password, status, rs.getLong(\"created_epoch_s\"));\n    }\n\n    /** Writes a re-derived credential for an existing account (transparent cost upgrade). */\n    synchronized void replacePasswordHash(long accountId, String newHash) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\"UPDATE account SET password = ? WHERE id = ?\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, newHash);\n            ps.setLong(2, accountId);\n            if (ps.executeUpdate() != 1) {\n                throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD, \"the account disappeared during rehash\");\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot store the rehashed password\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /** Server-side administrative disable; also the hook a password change would call. */\n    synchronized int setStatus(long accountId, String status) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        if (!\"active\".equals(status) && !\"disabled\".equals(status)) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD, \"refusing an unknown account status\");\n        }\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\"UPDATE account SET status = ? WHERE id = ?\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, status);\n            ps.setLong(2, accountId);\n            return ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot update the account status\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    synchronized int countAccounts() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        return countAll(\"account\");\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ throttling\n\n    /**\n     * Charges one failed authentication attempt against one bucket and reports whether the bucket\n     * is now in a penalty period.\n     *\n     * <p>Atomic: the counter is incremented <em>by the statement that reads it</em> - a single\n     * {@code UPDATE} whose {@code CASE} also rolls the window forward - inside a transaction, so\n     * the penalty is computed from the post-increment value the same transaction just wrote while\n     * holding the row lock. Two concurrent failures cannot both read {@code n} and both write\n     * {@code n + 1}, which would silently erase a penalty.\n     *\n     * <p>Fixed window with exponential back-off inside it; the window rolls and the counter resets\n     * once it lapses. A caller that arrives during a penalty is refused by {@link #isPenaltyActive}\n     * <em>before</em> this method runs, so an already-blocked client cannot extend its own penalty.\n     */\n    synchronized Throttle chargeFailure(String bucketKind, String canonicalKey, long nowEpochSeconds)\n            throws IdentityStoreException {\n        String bucket = bucketId(bucketKind, canonicalKey);\n        int window = config.authWindowSeconds();\n        int limit = BUCKET_KIND_ACCOUNT.equals(bucketKind)\n                ? config.authAccountMaxAttempts() : config.authSourceMaxAttempts();\n        long windowStartFloor = nowEpochSeconds - window;\n\n        boolean previousAutoCommit = true;\n        try {\n            previousAutoCommit = connection.getAutoCommit();\n            connection.setAutoCommit(false);\n\n            // Insert-then-update: a brand new bucket has no row to UPDATE. If two chargers race to\n            // insert, one gets a unique violation and retries as an update, so the net effect is\n            // still two charges.\n            int updated;\n            try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\"\"\"\n                    UPDATE auth_throttle\n                       SET failures = CASE WHEN first_at_epoch_s > ? THEN LEAST(failures + 1, ?) ELSE 1 END,\n                           first_at_epoch_s = CASE WHEN first_at_epoch_s > ? THEN first_at_epoch_s ELSE ? END,\n                           last_at_epoch_s = ?\n                     WHERE bucket = ?\"\"\")) {\n                ps.setLong(1, windowStartFloor);\n                ps.setInt(2, FAILURES_CEILING);\n                ps.setLong(3, windowStartFloor);\n                ps.setLong(4, nowEpochSeconds);\n                ps.setLong(5, nowEpochSeconds);\n                ps.setString(6, bucket);\n                updated = ps.executeUpdate();\n            }\n            if (updated == 0) {\n                try (PreparedStatement ins = connection.prepareStatement(\n                        \"INSERT INTO auth_throttle (bucket, failures, first_at_epoch_s, until_epoch_s, last_at_epoch_s)\"\n                                + \" VALUES (?, 1, ?, 0, ?)\")) {\n                    ins.setString(1, bucket);\n                    ins.setLong(2, nowEpochSeconds);\n                    ins.setLong(3, nowEpochSeconds);\n                    ins.executeUpdate();\n                } catch (SQLException raced) {\n                    if (!isUniqueViolation(raced)) {\n                        throw raced;\n                    }\n                    try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\"\"\"\n                            UPDATE auth_throttle\n                               SET failures = CASE WHEN first_at_epoch_s > ? THEN LEAST(failures + 1, ?) ELSE 1 END,\n                                   last_at_epoch_s = ?\n                             WHERE bucket = ?\"\"\")) {\n                        ps.setLong(1, windowStartFloor);\n                        ps.setInt(2, FAILURES_CEILING);\n                        ps.setLong(3, nowEpochSeconds);\n                        ps.setString(4, bucket);\n                        ps.executeUpdate();\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            int failures;\n            try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                    \"SELECT failures FROM auth_throttle WHERE bucket = ?\")) {\n                ps.setString(1, bucket);\n                try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                    failures = rs.next() ? rs.getInt(1) : 1;\n                }\n            }\n            int penaltySeconds = penaltySeconds(failures, limit, window, config.authPenaltyCeilingSeconds());\n            long until = penaltySeconds > 0 ? nowEpochSeconds + penaltySeconds : 0L;\n            try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                    \"UPDATE auth_throttle SET until_epoch_s = ? WHERE bucket = ?\")) {\n                ps.setLong(1, until);\n                ps.setString(2, bucket);\n                ps.executeUpdate();\n            }\n            connection.commit();\n            sweepThrottle(nowEpochSeconds);\n            return new Throttle(until > nowEpochSeconds, failures, penaltySeconds);\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            rollbackQuietly();\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot record the attempt\", e);\n        } finally {\n            restoreAutoCommit(previousAutoCommit);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /** True while a bucket is inside its penalty. Never creates or modifies a row. */\n    synchronized boolean isPenaltyActive(String bucketKind, String canonicalKey, long nowEpochSeconds)\n            throws IdentityStoreException {\n        Long until = readLongOrNull(\"SELECT until_epoch_s FROM auth_throttle WHERE bucket = ?\",\n                bucketId(bucketKind, canonicalKey));\n        return until != null && until > nowEpochSeconds;\n    }\n\n    /** Clears a bucket's counter and penalty, after a successful authentication. */\n    synchronized void clearBucket(String bucketKind, String canonicalKey) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\"DELETE FROM auth_throttle WHERE bucket = ?\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, bucketId(bucketKind, canonicalKey));\n            ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot clear the attempt counter\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Keeps the throttle table bounded. Rows that have lapsed are worthless, and without this an\n     * attacker could grow the database without limit by spraying identifiers.\n     */\n    private void sweepThrottle(long nowEpochSeconds) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        long horizon = config.authWindowSeconds() * 4L + 3600L;\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                \"DELETE FROM auth_throttle WHERE last_at_epoch_s < ? AND until_epoch_s < ?\")) {\n            ps.setLong(1, nowEpochSeconds - horizon);\n            ps.setLong(2, nowEpochSeconds - horizon);\n            ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot prune attempt counters\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /** Exponential back-off, capped twice: by the configured ceiling and by the window. */\n    private static int penaltySeconds(int failures, int limit, int windowSeconds, int ceiling) {\n        if (failures < limit) {\n            return 0;\n        }\n        int exponent = Math.min(failures - limit, 20); // keep the shift inside long range\n        long penalty = 1L << exponent;\n        penalty = Math.min(penalty, Math.min(ceiling, windowSeconds));\n        return (int) penalty;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ registration budgets\n\n    private record Budget(boolean exhausted, int used) {\n    }\n\n    private Budget readBudget(String bucketId, long now, int windowSeconds, int max) throws SQLException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                \"SELECT failures, first_at_epoch_s FROM auth_throttle WHERE bucket = ?\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, bucketId);\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                if (!rs.next()) {\n                    return new Budget(false, 0);\n                }\n                int failures = rs.getInt(1);\n                long firstAt = rs.getLong(2);\n                if (firstAt <= now - windowSeconds) {\n                    return new Budget(false, 0); // window lapsed: treated as empty\n                }\n                return new Budget(failures >= max, failures);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    private void chargeBudget(String bucketId, long now, int windowSeconds) throws SQLException {\n        long floor = now - windowSeconds;\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\"\"\"\n                UPDATE auth_throttle\n                   SET failures = CASE WHEN first_at_epoch_s > ? THEN LEAST(failures + 1, ?) ELSE 1 END,\n                       first_at_epoch_s = CASE WHEN first_at_epoch_s > ? THEN first_at_epoch_s ELSE ? END,\n                       last_at_epoch_s = ?\n                 WHERE bucket = ?\"\"\")) {\n            ps.setLong(1, floor);\n            ps.setInt(2, FAILURES_CEILING);\n            ps.setLong(3, floor);\n            ps.setLong(4, now);\n            ps.setLong(5, now);\n            ps.setString(6, bucketId);\n            if (ps.executeUpdate() == 0) {\n                try (PreparedStatement ins = connection.prepareStatement(\n                        \"INSERT INTO auth_throttle (bucket, failures, first_at_epoch_s, until_epoch_s, last_at_epoch_s)\"\n                                + \" VALUES (?, 1, ?, 0, ?)\")) {\n                    ins.setString(1, bucketId);\n                    ins.setLong(2, now);\n                    ins.setLong(3, now);\n                    ins.executeUpdate();\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ sessions\n\n    /**\n     * Issues a session and enforces the per-account cap in one transaction.\n     *\n     * <p>The cap is one self-converging {@code DELETE} that keeps the newest N rows, not\n     * count-then-truncate: two concurrent logins both leave the table satisfying the cap, and\n     * neither can leave {@code N + 1} live sessions behind.\n     *\n     * <p>The token comes from {@link SessionToken#generate} ({@link SecureRandom}) and is never\n     * accepted from the caller; the row is keyed by its SHA-256 digest, so reading this table does\n     * not hand over usable credentials.\n     */\n    synchronized void createSession(long accountId, SessionToken token, long nowEpochSeconds)\n            throws IdentityStoreException {\n        long expires = nowEpochSeconds + config.sessionTtlSeconds();\n        boolean previousAutoCommit = true;\n        try {\n            previousAutoCommit = connection.getAutoCommit();\n            connection.setAutoCommit(false);\n            try (PreparedStatement ins = connection.prepareStatement(\n                    \"INSERT INTO session (token_hash, account_id, created_at_epoch_s, expires_at_epoch_s)\"\n                            + \" VALUES (?,?,?,?)\")) {\n                ins.setString(1, token.tokenHash());\n                ins.setLong(2, accountId);\n                ins.setLong(3, nowEpochSeconds);\n                ins.setLong(4, expires);\n                if (ins.executeUpdate() != 1) {\n                    throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"the session row was not written\");\n                }\n            } catch (SQLException e) {\n                connection.rollback();\n                if (isUniqueViolation(e)) {\n                    // A collision on a 256-bit CSPRNG value means the random source is broken, not\n                    // that someone signed in twice. Fail closed; do not paper over it.\n                    throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CRYPTO_FAILURE,\n                            \"the generated session token collided with an existing one\", e);\n                }\n                throw e;\n            }\n            try (PreparedStatement prune = connection.prepareStatement(\n                    \"DELETE FROM session WHERE account_id = ? AND token_hash NOT IN (\"\n                            + \"SELECT token_hash FROM session WHERE account_id = ?\"\n                            + \" ORDER BY created_at_epoch_s DESC, token_hash DESC FETCH FIRST ? ROWS ONLY)\")) {\n                prune.setLong(1, accountId);\n                prune.setLong(2, accountId);\n                prune.setInt(3, config.maxSessionsPerAccount());\n                prune.executeUpdate();\n            }\n            connection.commit();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            rollbackQuietly();\n            if (e instanceof IdentityStoreException ise) {\n                throw ise;\n            }\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot create the session\", e);\n        } finally {\n            restoreAutoCommit(previousAutoCommit);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Resolves a submitted token to a session row in one statement, returning the server-side state\n     * (expiry, account status) the caller must check. Nothing on the row is trusted as proof of\n     * identity beyond the token itself, and the token is never echoed.\n     */\n    synchronized SessionRow resolveSession(SessionToken token, long nowEpochSeconds) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        String sql = \"SELECT s.expires_at_epoch_s, a.id, a.username_canon, a.status\"\n                + \" FROM session s JOIN account a ON a.id = s.account_id WHERE s.token_hash = ?\";\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(sql)) {\n            ps.setString(1, token.tokenHash());\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                if (!rs.next()) {\n                    return null;\n                }\n                Identity username = Identity.fromStoredUsername(rs.getString(\"username_canon\"));\n                if (username == null) {\n                    throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD,\n                            \"the session points at an account with an invalid username\");\n                }\n                long expires = rs.getLong(1);\n                return new SessionRow(rs.getLong(2), username, rs.getString(3), expires, expires > nowEpochSeconds);\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot read the session\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Deletes a session; 1 if it was live, 0 if there was nothing to delete. Both are reported to\n     * the caller as {@link Reason#SESSION_REVOKED} - the count is for the audit log only.\n     */\n    synchronized int revokeSession(SessionToken token) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\"DELETE FROM session WHERE token_hash = ?\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, token.tokenHash());\n            return ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot revoke the session\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /** Revokes every session for an account in one statement, so there is no partial window. */\n    synchronized int revokeAllSessions(long accountId) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\"DELETE FROM session WHERE account_id = ?\")) {\n            ps.setLong(1, accountId);\n            return ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot revoke sessions\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Removes sessions whose TTL elapsed. A session row is deleted rather than merely judged dead\n     * on read, so a dump of the database overstates nothing - and a revoked token stops being\n     * replayable even if a future bug forgets the expiry check.\n     */\n    synchronized int deleteExpiredSessions(long nowEpochSeconds) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                \"DELETE FROM session WHERE expires_at_epoch_s <= ?\")) {\n            return ps.executeUpdate();\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot prune sessions\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    synchronized int countSessions() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        return countAll(\"session\");\n    }\n\n    synchronized int countThrottleRows() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        return countAll(\"auth_throttle\");\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers\n\n    /** Immutable row of {@code account}, re-validated. The hash is never printed or compared here. */\n    record Account(long id, Identity username, Identity email, String passwordHash, String status,\n                   long createdEpochSeconds) {\n        @Override\n        public String toString() {\n            return \"Account[id=\" + id + \", \" + username + \", status=\" + status + \"]\";\n        }\n    }\n\n    record SessionRow(long accountId, Identity username, String status, long expiresAtEpochSeconds, boolean live) {\n        @Override\n        public String toString() {\n            return \"SessionRow[account=\" + accountId + \", live=\" + live + \"]\";\n        }\n    }\n\n    record Throttle(boolean blocked, int failures, int penaltySeconds) {\n    }\n\n    record Outcome(Reason reason, SessionToken token) {\n    }\n\n    private int countAll(String table) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        // table is a literal at every call site; no caller data reaches this string.\n        try (Statement s = connection.createStatement();\n             ResultSet rs = s.executeQuery(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM \" + table)) {\n            return rs.next() ? rs.getInt(1) : 0;\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot count rows\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    private Long readLongOrNull(String sql, String param) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(sql)) {\n            ps.setString(1, param);\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                return rs.next() ? rs.getLong(1) : null;\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot read the attempt counter\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    private boolean existsCanonical(String column, String canonical) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        // column is one of two literals chosen in code, never input.\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = connection.prepareStatement(\n                \"SELECT 1 FROM account WHERE \" + column + \" = ?\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, canonical);\n            try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n                return rs.next();\n            }\n        } catch (SQLException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, \"cannot resolve the collision\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    private static boolean isUniqueViolation(SQLException e) {\n        // SQLState class 23 is integrity constraint violation. Classified on the state, not on\n        // message text: a localised or reworded driver message must not turn a real storage failure\n        // into a silently-swallowed \"duplicate\".\n        String state = e.getSQLState();\n        return state != null && state.startsWith(\"23\");\n    }\n\n    private void rollbackQuietly() {\n        try {\n            connection.rollback();\n        } catch (SQLException ignored) {\n            // A failed rollback leaves the transaction to be discarded on close.\n        }\n    }\n\n    private void restoreAutoCommit(boolean previous) {\n        try {\n            connection.setAutoCommit(previous);\n        } catch (SQLException ignored) {\n            // Single-use connection per process; nothing actionable.\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ bucket keys\n\n    private static byte[] loadOrCreateBucketKey(Connection c) throws SQLException, IdentityStoreException {\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = c.prepareStatement(\"SELECT v FROM meta WHERE k = 'bucket-key'\");\n             ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) {\n            if (rs.next()) {\n                String stored = rs.getString(1);\n                if (stored != null && stored.length() == 43) {\n                    try {\n                        byte[] raw = Base64.getUrlDecoder().decode(stored);\n                        if (raw.length == 32) {\n                            return raw;\n                        }\n                    } catch (IllegalArgumentException notBase64) {\n                        // Replace it below.\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        byte[] fresh = new byte[32];\n        new SecureRandom().nextBytes(fresh);\n        try (PreparedStatement ps = c.prepareStatement(\"MERGE INTO meta (k, v) KEY(k) VALUES ('bucket-key', ?)\")) {\n            ps.setString(1, Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(fresh));\n            ps.executeUpdate();\n        }\n        return fresh;\n    }\n\n    /** Fixed-width keyed bucket id; no identifier plaintext is stored in the throttle table. */\n    private String bucketId(String kind, String canonicalValue) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        if (kind == null || kind.isEmpty() || canonicalValue == null) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CORRUPT_RECORD, \"refusing an incomplete bucket key\");\n        }\n        try {\n            Mac mac = Mac.getInstance(\"HmacSHA256\");\n            SecretKeySpec key = new SecretKeySpec(bucketKey, \"HmacSHA256\");\n            try {\n                mac.init(key);\n                mac.update((byte) kind.charAt(0));\n                byte[] digest = mac.doFinal(canonicalValue.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));\n                return kind + \":\" + Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(digest);\n            } finally {\n                key.clearPassword();\n            }\n        } catch (java.security.GeneralSecurityException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.CRYPTO_FAILURE, \"cannot key the attempt A candidate we refuse to hash is rejected <em>with a\n *     derivation's cost</em> (see below), never cheaply - otherwise \"is this password long enough\"\n *     becomes an unauthenticated oracle.</li>\n *   <li><b>Penalty windows</b> third, keyed by the <em>canonical identifier</em> whether or not an\n *     account exists for it. This is what makes the limits non-weaponisable: the counter is global\n *     across sources (so spraying sources cannot lock a legitimate user out - Rule 3), and because\n *     a blocked client is refused <em>before</em> any lookup, it cannot extend its own penalty.</li>\n *   <li><b>Account lookup</b> fourth.</li>\n *   <li><b>Password verification</b> fifth.</li>\n *   <li><b>Account status</b> <em>after</em> verification. Reading {@code status} before the\n *     password check would let an unauthenticated caller learn which accounts are administratively\n *     disabled, both from the message and from the timing of an early return.</li>\n *   <li><b>Session issue</b> last.</li>\n * </ol>\n *\n * <h2>Equal work on every refusal (Rule 6)</h2>\n * Every branch that could distinguish \"this identifier exists\" from \"it does not\" pays roughly one\n * PBKDF2 derivation: unknown account, corrupt row, wrong password, and a candidate that fails\n * policy all do. {@link PasswordHasher#chargeDummy} spends the work when there is nothing real to\n * verify. The throttled branch is the one deliberate exception, and it is not an oracle: the same\n * cheap refusal is available whether the identifier exists or not, because the bucket was created\n * by the earlier failures either way. Charging the derivation there would defeat a limiter whose\n * entire purpose is to bound that cost.\n *\n * <h2>What this class never does</h2>\n * It never logs, prints, returns or stores the plaintext password, the stored hash, the salt, or\n * the iteration count. It never trusts {@code display}: every string it echoes back was re-read\n * from the database and re-validated. It never decides an outcome from a caller-supplied\n * identifier, token, or role.\n */\npublic final class AuthApi implements AutoCloseable {\n\n    private final SqlIdentityStore store;\n    private final PasswordHasher hasher;\n    private final AuditLog audit;\n    private final Config config;\n    private final TimeSource time;\n    private final SecureRandom random = new SecureRandom();\n\n    public AuthApi(SqlIdentityStore store, PasswordHasher hasher, AuditLog audit, Config config,\n                   TimeSource time) {\n        this.store = store;\n        this.hasher = hasher;\n        this.audit = audit;\n        this.config = config;\n        this.time = time;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ registration\n\n    /**\n     * Registers an account.\n     *\n     * @param sourceLabel asserted origin, validated by {@link SourceId#parse}; A caller already over budget is refused there.\n        try {\n            String hash = hasher.hash(password); // erases the password\n            SqlIdentityStore.Outcome outcome = store.register(username.canonical(), username,\n                    email, email.canonical(), hash);\n            // The display form stored is the canonical one; echoing raw input back would put\n            // caller bytes into whatever the caller does with the result.\n            audit.append(outcome.reason(), username);\n            return AuthResult.of(outcome.reason());\n        } catch (IdentityStoreException e) {\n            closeQuietly(password);\n            audit.append(e.reason(), username);\n            throw e;\n        } finally {\n            closeQuietly(password);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ sign-in\n\n    /**\n     * Verifies a credential and, on success, issues a session.\n     *\n     * <p>Never call this with a password taken from a command-line argument or an environment\n     * variable - see {@link PortalCli} for the two accepted input paths.\n     */\n    public AuthResult signIn(String identifierRaw, char[] passwordChars, String sourceLabel)\n            throws IdentityStoreException {\n        long now = time.nowEpochSeconds();\n        SourceId source = SourceId.parse(sourceLabel);\n        if (source == null) {\n            // Abort before doing any work, so an invalid source is not a way to make the server\n            // derive a key for free.\n            Password.erase(passwordChars);\n            audit.append(Reason.INVALID_REQUEST, null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_REQUEST);\n        }\n\n        Identity identifier = parseIdentifier(identifierRaw);\n\n        // Policy check before hashing. identifier.canonical(), now);\n        if (sourceBlocked || accountBlocked) {\n            Password.erase(passwordChars);\n            audit.append(Reason.THROTTLED, identifier);\n            return chargeEqualWork(password.chars());\n            Password.erase(passwordChars);\n            chargeBothBuckets(source, identifier, now);\n            audit.append(Reason.ABSENT_ACCOUNT, identifier);\n It never decides an outcome from a caller-supplied token, identifier\n * mapping, or role.\n */\npublic final class AuthApi implements AutoCloseable {\n\n    private final SqlIdentityStore store;\n    private final PasswordHasher hasher;\n    private final AuditLog audit;\n    private final Config config;\n    private final TimeSource time;\n    private final SecureRandom random = new SecureRandom();\n\n    public AuthApi(SqlIdentityStore store, PasswordHasher hasher, AuditLog audit, Config config,\n                   TimeSource time) {\n        this.store = store;\n        this.hasher = hasher;\n        this.audit = audit;\n        this.config = config;\n        this.time = time;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ registration\n\n    /**\n     * Registers an account.\n     *\n     * @param passwordChars consumed and erased on every path, including the rejected ones\n     * @param sourceLabel   asserted origin; see {@link SourceId} for why it is treated as hostile\n     */\n    public AuthResult register(String emailRaw, String usernameRaw, char[] passwordChars, String sourceLabel)\n            throws IdentityStoreException {\n        // Validation first, before any secret is touched: these outcomes are about the caller's own\n        // input and are allowed to be specific, because none of them says whether an account exists.\n        SourceId source = SourceId.parse(sourceLabel);\n        if (source == null) {\n            Password.erase(passwordChars);\n            audit.append(Reason.INVALID_REQUEST, null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_REQUEST);\n        }\n        Identity email = Identity.parseClientEmail(emailRaw);\n        if (email == null) {\n            Password.erase(passwordChars);\n            audit.append(Reason.INVALID_EMAIL, null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_EMAIL);\n        }\n        Identity username = Identity.parseClientUsername(usernameRaw);\n        if (username == null) {\n            Password.erase(passwordChars);\n            audit.append(Reason.INVALID_USERNAME, null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_USERNAME);\n        }\n        Password password = Password.adopt(passwordChars); // erases the array if it is rejected\n        if (password == null) {\n            audit.append(Reason.INVALID_PASSWORD, username);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_PASSWORD);\n        }\n\n        try {\n            String hash = hasher.hash(password); // closes the password\n            // Budgets and the account cap are enforced inside the store's transaction, behind the\n            // serialisation row, so neither can be raced.\n            SqlIdentityStore.Outcome outcome =\n                    store.register(username.canonical(), username, email, email.canonical(), hash);\n            audit.append(outcome.reason(), username);\n            return AuthResult.of(outcome.reason());\n        } catch (IdentityStoreException e) {\n            password.close();\n            audit.append(e.reason(), username);\n            throw e;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ sign-in\n\n    /**\n     * Verifies a credential and, on success, issues a session.\n     *\n     * @param passwordChars consumed and erased on every path\n     */\n    public AuthResult signIn(String identifierRaw, char[] passwordChars, String sourceLabel)\n            throws IdentityStoreException {\n        long now = time.nowEpochSeconds();\n\n        SourceId source = SourceId.parse(sourceLabel);\n        if (source == null) {\n            Password.erase(passwordChars);\n            audit.append(Reason.INVALID_REQUEST, null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_REQUEST);\n        }\n\n        Identity identifier = parseIdentifier(identifierRaw);\n        Password password = Password.adopt(passwordChars);\n\n        Password held = password; // for the finally block; `password` may be closed early below\n        try {\n            // (2) Policy. Refused at verification cost, so password policy is not an oracle.\n            if (held == null) {\n                chargeEqualWork();\n                if (identifier != null) {\n                    chargeBothBuckets(source, identifier, now);\n                }\n                audit.append(Reason.INVALID_PASSWORD, identifier);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            // A malformed identifier never reaches the database. Equal cost, same message.\n            if (identifier == null) {\n                chargeEqualWork();\n                audit.append(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL, null);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            // (3) Penalties, before any read or write.\n            boolean sourceBlocked =\n                    store.isPenaltyActive(SqlIdentityStore.bucketKindSource(), source.canonical(), now);\n            boolean accountBlocked =\n                    store.isPenaltyActive(SqlIdentityStore.bucketKindAccount(), identifier.canonical(), now);\n            if (sourceBlocked || accountBlocked) {\n                audit.append(Reason.THROTTLED, identifier);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            // (4) Lookup. A row that fails strict re-validation is a storage fact, not a user fact:\n            // it becomes the same outcome as \"no such account\".\n            SqlIdentityStore.Account account;\n            try {\n                account = store.findByCanonicalIdentity(identifier);\n            } catch (IdentityStoreException corrupt) {\n                chargeEqualWork();\n                audit.append(Reason.ROW_REJECTED_AS_ABSENT_EVENT, identifier);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            if (account == null) {\n                chargeEqualWork();\n                chargeBothBuckets(source, identifier, now);\n                audit.append(Reason.ABSENT_ACCOUNT, identifier);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            // (5) Verify.\n            boolean ok = hasher.matchesStored(held.chars(), account.passwordHash());\n            if (!ok) {\n                chargeBothBuckets(source, identifier, now);\n                audit.append(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL, identifier);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            // (6) Status, only now that the credential is proven.\n            if (!\"active\".equals(account.status())) {\n                store.clearBucket(SqlIdentityStore.bucketKindAccount(), identifier.canonical());\n                audit.append(Reason.ACCOUNT_DISABLED, identifier);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            // Verified: reset the per-account counter. The per-source counter is deliberately left\n            // alone - clearing it on success would let an attacker who knows one real credential\n            // keep their source bucket permanently empty by alternating a correct login with a\n            // thousand guesses.\n            store.clearBucket(SqlIdentityStore.bucketKindAccount(), identifier.canonical());\n\n            // (7) Transparent cost upgrade, while the candidate is still in hand. Re-encoding is a\n            // credential change, so outstanding sessions are revoked with it: a token stolen before\n            // the upgrade cannot outlive it.\n            if (hasher.needsRehash(account.passwordHash())) {\n                try {\n                    Password forRehash = Password.copyOf(held.chars());\n                    if (forRehash != null) {\n                        store.replacePasswordHash(account.id(), hasher.hash(forRehash));\n                        store.revokeAllSessions(account.id());\n                        audit.appendEvent(AuditEvent.CREDENTIAL_REENCODED);\n                    }\n                } catch (IdentityStoreException e) {\n                    // The user did authenticate. Failing the upgrade must not refuse them - the old\n                    // parameters still verify - so the reason is logged and sign-in proceeds.\n                    audit.append(e.reason(), identifier);\n                }\n            }\n\n            SessionToken token = SessionToken.generate(random);\n            store.createSession(account.id(), token, now);\n            store.deleteExpiredSessions(now);\n            audit.append(Reason.AUTHENTICATED, identifier);\n            return AuthResult.success(Reason.AUTHENTICATED, token, account.username().canonical());\n        } finally {\n            if (held != null) {\n                held.close();\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ sessions\n\n    /**\n     * Resolves a submitted token against server-side state. Rule 3: a token is a lookup key, not\n     * proof. The account's live status is re-read from the row every call, so disabling an account\n     * takes effect immediately rather than at the token's next expiry.\n     */\n    public AuthResult checkSession(String tokenRaw) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        long now = time.nowEpochSeconds();\n        SessionToken token = SessionToken.parse(tokenRaw);\n        if (token == null) {\n            // Wrong shape: refuse without a query, so junk cannot be used to probe and costs\n            // nothing. Same message as an unknown token, so the shape check is not an oracle.\n            audit.append(Reason.MALFORMED_TOKEN, null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_SESSION);\n        }\n        SqlIdentityStore.SessionRow row;\n        try {\n            row = store.resolveSession(token, now);\n        } catch (IdentityStoreException corrupt) {\n            audit.append(corrupt.reason(), null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_SESSION);\n        }\n        if (row == null || !row.live()) {\n            audit.append(Reason.INVALID_SESSION, null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_SESSION);\n        }\n        if (!\"active\".equals(row.status())) {\n            store.revokeSession(token);\n            audit.append(Reason.INVALID_SESSION, row.username());\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_SESSION);\n        }\n        return AuthResult.success(Reason.AUTHENTICATED, null, row.username().canonical());\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Revokes one session. The user-visible message is identical whether or not the token was live,\n     * so this is not a token-existence oracle; the distinction is kept for the operator.\n     */\n    public AuthResult revokeSession(String tokenRaw) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        SessionToken token = SessionToken.parse(tokenRaw);\n        if (token == null) {\n            audit.append(Reason.MALFORMED_TOKEN, null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.SESSION_REVOKED);\n        }\n        int removed = store.revokeSession(token);\n        audit.append(removed > 0 ? Reason.SESSION_REVOKED : Reason.ALREADY_REVOKED, null);\n        return AuthResult.of(Reason.SESSION_REVOKED);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ administration\n\n    /**\n     * Changes an account's administrative status and revokes its sessions when disabling. Server-side\n     * state, reachable only through this in-process call - no unauthenticated path exposes it, and\n     * {@link #signIn} will not tell a caller it happened.\n     */\n    public AuthResult setAccountStatus(Identity username, String status) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        SqlIdentityStore.Account account = store.findByCanonicalIdentity(username);\n        if (account == null) {\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.ABSENT_ACCOUNT);\n        }\n        store.setStatus(account.id(), status);\n        if (!\"active\".equals(status)) {\n            store.revokeAllSessions(account.id());\n        }\n        audit.appendEvent(AuditEvent.STATUS_CHANGED);\n        return AuthResult.of(Reason.ACCOUNT_CREATED);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ operational reads\n\n    public int liveSessionCount() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        store.deleteExpiredSessions(time.nowEpochSeconds());\n        return store.countSessions();\n    }\n\n    public int accountCount() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        return store.countAccounts();\n    }\n\n    public int throttleRowCount() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        return store.countThrottleRows();\n    }\n\n    public java.util.List<String> startupWarnings() {\n        return store.startupWarnings();\n    }\n\n    /** For tests: the validated config in force. Never contains a user secret. */\n    public Config config() {\n        return config;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers\n\n    /** An identifier may be either form. Whichever parses, parses; never a merge of the two. */\n    private static Identity parseIdentifier(String raw) {\n        Identity byEmail = Identity.parseClientEmail(raw);\n        if (byEmail != null) {\n            return byEmail;\n        }\n        return Identity.parseClientUsername(raw);\n    }\n\n    private void chargeEqualWork() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        // Propagates rather than swallowing: if the JCE lost PBKDF2, the equal-work guarantee is\n        // gone and a refusal must not quietly become a success path.\n        hasher.chargeDummy();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Charges source then account. Refused at verification cost, so password policy is not an oracle.\n            if (password == null) {\n                chargeEqualWork();\n                if (identifier != null) {\n                    chargeBothBuckets(source, identifier, now);\n                }\n                audit.append(Reason.INVALID_PASSWORD, identifier);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            // A malformed identifier never reaches the database. Equal cost, same message.\n            if (identifier == null) {\n                chargeEqualWork();\n                audit.append(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL, null);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            // (3) Penalties, before any read or write.\n            boolean sourceBlocked =\n                    store.isPenaltyActive(SqlIdentityStore.bucketKindSource(), source.canonical(), now);\n            boolean accountBlocked =\n                    store.isPenaltyActive(SqlIdentityStore.bucketKindAccount(), identifier.canonical(), now);\n            if (sourceBlocked || accountBlocked) {\n                audit.append(Reason.THROTTLED, identifier);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            // (4) Lookup. A row that fails strict re-validation is a storage fact, not a user fact:\n            // it becomes the same outcome as \"no such account\".\n            SqlIdentityStore.Account account;\n            try {\n                account = store.findByCanonicalIdentity(identifier);\n            } catch (IdentityStoreException corrupt) {\n                chargeEqualWork();\n                audit.appendEvent(AuditEvent.ROW_REJECTED_AS_ABSENT);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            if (account == null) {\n                chargeEqualWork();\n                chargeBothBuckets(source, identifier, now);\n                audit.append(Reason.ABSENT_ACCOUNT, identifier);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            // (5) Verify.\n            boolean ok = hasher.matchesStored(password.chars(), account.passwordHash());\n            if (!ok) {\n                chargeBothBuckets(source, identifier, now);\n                audit.append(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL, identifier);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            // (6) Status, only now that the credential is proven.\n            if (!\"active\".equals(account.status())) {\n                store.clearBucket(SqlIdentityStore.bucketKindAccount(), identifier.canonical());\n                audit.append(Reason.ACCOUNT_DISABLED, identifier);\n                return AuthResult.of(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            }\n\n            // Verified: reset the per-account counter. The per-source counter is deliberately left\n            // alone - clearing it on success would let an attacker who knows one real credential\n            // keep their source bucket permanently empty by alternating a correct login with a\n            // thousand guesses.\n            store.clearBucket(SqlIdentityStore.bucketKindAccount(), identifier.canonical());\n\n            // (7) Transparent cost upgrade, while the candidate is still in hand. Re-encoding is a\n            // credential change, so outstanding sessions are revoked with it: a token stolen before\n            // the upgrade cannot outlive it.\n            if (hasher.needsRehash(account.passwordHash())) {\n                try {\n                    Password forRehash = Password.copyOf(password.chars());\n                    if (forRehash != null) {\n                        store.replacePasswordHash(account.id(), hasher.hash(forRehash));\n                        store.revokeAllSessions(account.id());\n                        audit.appendEvent(AuditEvent.CREDENTIAL_REENCODED);\n                    }\n                } catch (IdentityStoreException e) {\n                    // The user did authenticate. Failing the upgrade must not refuse them - the old\n                    // parameters still verify - so the reason is logged and sign-in proceeds.\n                    audit.append(e.reason(), identifier);\n                }\n            }\n\n            SessionToken token = SessionToken.generate(random);\n            store.createSession(account.id(), token, now);\n            store.deleteExpiredSessions(now);\n            audit.append(Reason.AUTHENTICATED, identifier);\n            return AuthResult.success(Reason.AUTHENTICATED, token, account.username().canonical());\n        } finally {\n            if (password != null) {\n                password.close();\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ sessions\n\n    /**\n     * Resolves a submitted token against server-side state. Rule 3: a token is a lookup key, not\n     * proof. The account's live status is re-read from the row every call, so disabling an account\n     * takes effect immediately rather than at the token's next expiry.\n     */\n    public AuthResult checkSession(String tokenRaw) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        long now = time.nowEpochSeconds();\n        SessionToken token = SessionToken.parse(tokenRaw);\n        if (token == null) {\n            // Wrong shape: refuse without a query, so junk cannot be used to probe and costs\n            // nothing. Same message as an unknown token, so the shape check is not an oracle.\n            audit.append(Reason.MALFORMED_TOKEN, null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_SESSION);\n        }\n        SqlIdentityStore.SessionRow row;\n        try {\n            row = store.resolveSession(token, now);\n        } catch (IdentityStoreException corrupt) {\n            audit.append(corrupt.reason(), null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_SESSION);\n        }\n        if (row == null || !row.live()) {\n            audit.append(Reason.INVALID_SESSION, null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_SESSION);\n        }\n        if (!\"active\".equals(row.status())) {\n            store.revokeSession(token);\n            audit.append(Reason.INVALID_SESSION, row.username());\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.INVALID_SESSION);\n        }\n        return AuthResult.success(Reason.AUTHENTICATED, null, row.username().canonical());\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Revokes one session. The user-visible message is identical whether or not the token was live,\n     * so this is not a token-existence oracle; the distinction is kept for the operator.\n     */\n    public AuthResult revokeSession(String tokenRaw) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        SessionToken token = SessionToken.parse(tokenRaw);\n        if (token == null) {\n            audit.append(Reason.MALFORMED_TOKEN, null);\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.SESSION_REVOKED);\n        }\n        int removed = store.revokeSession(token);\n        audit.append(removed > 0 ? Reason.SESSION_REVOKED : Reason.ALREADY_REVOKED, null);\n        return AuthResult.of(Reason.SESSION_REVOKED);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ administration\n\n    /**\n     * Changes an account's administrative status and revokes its sessions when disabling. Reachable\n     * only in-process: no unauthenticated path exposes it, and {@link #signIn} will not tell a\n     * caller it happened.\n     */\n    public AuthResult setAccountStatus(Identity username, String status) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        SqlIdentityStore.Account account = store.findByCanonicalIdentity(username);\n        if (account == null) {\n            return AuthResult.of(Reason.ABSENT_ACCOUNT);\n        }\n        store.setStatus(account.id(), status);\n        if (!\"active\".equals(status)) {\n            store.revokeAllSessions(account.id());\n        }\n        audit.appendEvent(AuditEvent.STATUS_CHANGED);\n        return AuthResult.of(Reason.ACCOUNT_CREATED);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ operational reads\n\n    public int liveSessionCount() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        store.deleteExpiredSessions(time.nowEpochSeconds());\n        return store.countSessions();\n    }\n\n    public int accountCount() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        return store.countAccounts();\n    }\n\n    public int throttleRowCount() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        return store.countThrottleRows();\n    }\n\n    public java.util.List<String> startupWarnings() {\n        return store.startupWarnings();\n    }\n\n    /** For tests: the validated config in force. Never contains a user secret. */\n    public Config config() {\n        return config;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers\n\n    /** An identifier may be either form. Whichever parses, parses; never a merge of the two. */\n    private static Identity parseIdentifier(String raw) {\n        Identity byEmail = Identity.parseClientEmail(raw);\n        if (byEmail != null) {\n            return byEmail;\n        }\n        return Identity.parseClientUsername(raw);\n    }\n\n    private void chargeEqualWork() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        // Propagates rather than swallowing: if the JCE lost PBKDF2 the equal-work guarantee is\n        // gone, and a refusal must not quietly become a success path.\n        hasher.chargeDummy();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Charges source then account. It ships no Argon2, scrypt or bcrypt, and pulling in a native\n * crypto library to replace a JCE primitive that meets the current OWASP minimum would add supply\n * chain risk without adding strength. So: platform primitives only, zero third-party crypto.\n * <p>The iteration floor is set to the OWASP 2025 minimum for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (600,000). That\n * was measured on this machine at roughly 850 ms per derivation, which is the price of one\n * registration or one sign-in, and is paid once per request by every branch including refusals.\n * The value lives in {@link Config}, is validated on read, and is upgraded by re-encoding on\n * successful sign-in ({@link #needsRehash}) rather than by editing a constant nobody notices.\n *\n * <h2>Stored encoding</h2>\n * {@code v1$pbkdf2-sha256$<iterations>$<salt-b64>$<digest-b64>} - all ASCII, no whitespace, no\n * {@code $} inside a field, bounded length. {@link #decode} is strict enough to be a\n * fail-closed boundary in its own right: a corrupt, truncated, over-long or low-iteration row is\n * refused, and the caller then answers with the same generic refusal it uses for a wrong password.\n * This matters because the {@code iterations} field is read from the database and therefore\n * attacker-controlled: an unvalidated field would let anyone who can write a row set\n * {@code iterations=1} and make the KDF effectively free. {@link #decode} refuses it.\n *\n * <h2>Constant time</h2>\n * Comparison uses {@link MessageDigest#isEqual} over derived digests. Everything the CLI does, a front end would do through\n * here - which is the point: one place makes the security decisions, so a second transport cannot\n * accidentally skip a check.\n *\n * <h2>The order of checks in {@link #signIn} <em>is</em> the security property</h2>\n * <ol>\n *   <li><b>Source label</b> first. An unusable label aborts the request before any lookup or\n *     derivation, so it is never a way to get work done for free and never a bucket to hide\n *     behind.</li>\n *   <li><b>Password policy</b> second. A candidate we refuse to hash is rejected <em>at a\n *     derivation's cost</em>, never cheaply - otherwise \"is this password long enough\" becomes an\n *     unauthenticated oracle.</li>\n *   <li><b>Penalty windows</b> third, keyed by the <em>canonical identifier</em> whether or not an\n *     account exists for it. This is what keeps our own limit from being weaponised (Rule 3): the\n *     per-account counter is global across sources, so spraying sources cannot lock a real user out\n *     of their own account; and because a blocked caller is refused <em>before</em> any lookup or\n *     write, it cannot extend its own penalty.</li>\n *   <li><b>Account lookup</b> fourth.</li>\n *   <li><b>Password verification</b> fifth.</li>\n *   <li><b>Account status</b> <em>after</em> verification. Charging the derivation there would defeat a limiter whose whole\n * purpose is to bound that cost. There is no\n * free-text field into which a caller could concatenate a password, and no accessor exists that\n * accepts an arbitrary string. This is stronger than scrubbing, because scrubbing depends on\n * guessing every shape a secret can take; the writer never receives one to begin with.\n *\n * <h2>Scrubbing is the second control, and it is tested against the shapes that defeat the naive\n * version</h2>\n * If a future change ever does route text here, {@link #scrub} catches it. Two specific traps were\n * avoided: word-boundary matching, which never matches {@code AUTH_DB_PASSWORD=} because\n * {@code _} is a word character; and {@code \\S+} value matching, which leaks the tail of a\n * passphrase containing a space. Both cases are in the test suite.\n *\n * <h2>Failure behaviour</h2>\n * An unwritable log is a hard failure, not a warning: the audit trail is part of what makes a\n * security decision defensible, so {@link #append} throws and the caller fails closed. It is\n * deliberately <em>not</em> remembered as a latched \"degraded\" flag - a flag set once and never\n * cleared turns one transient failure into a permanent outage. Each call re-evaluates the file, so\n * the service recovers as soon as the filesystem does; {@code AuditLogRecoveryTest} asserts that.\n *\n * <h2>File discipline</h2>\n * Created 0600 and verified by reading the permission set back - our own process running as root\n * can read a {@code 0000} file, so a successful write proves nothing about who else can read it.\n * A symlink at the target path is refused rather than followed, which is what stops the path being\n * redirected at {@code ~/.ssh/authorized_keys} by whoever can create that file first. Size is\n * capped; past the cap, appends stop and the fact is reported on stderr, because silently growing\n * an unbounded file under a security event flood is a disk-exhaustion DoS.\n */\nfinal class AuditLog implements AutoCloseable {\n\n    private static final String FILE_NAME = \"audit.log\";\n\n    private final Path file;\n    private final long maxBytes;\n    private boolean warnedAboutCap;\n\n    AuditLog(Config config) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        this(config.dataDir().resolve(FILE_NAME), config.auditMaxBytes(), config.auditRequirePrivateFile());\n    }\n\n    AuditLog(Path file, long maxBytes, boolean requirePrivate) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        this.file = file;\n        this.maxBytes = maxBytes;\n        PosixFiles.createPrivateDir(file.getParent());\n        if (Files.exists(file, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {\n            if (Files.isSymbolicLink(file)) {\n                throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.AUDIT_FAILURE,\n                        \"the audit log path is a symbolic link and will not be followed\");\n            }\n            if (!Files.isRegularFile(file, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {\n                throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.AUDIT_FAILURE,\n                        \"the audit log path exists and is not a regular file\");\n            }\n        } else {\n            try {\n                Files.createFile(file, java.nio.file.attribute.PosixFilePermissions.asFileAttribute(\n                        PosixFiles.PRIVATE_FILE));\n            } catch (UnsupportedOperationException noPosix) {\n                throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.AUDIT_FAILURE,\n                        \"the filesystem hosting the audit log does not support POSIX permissions\", noPosix);\n            } catch (IOException e) {\n                throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.AUDIT_FAILURE, \"cannot create the audit log\", e);\n            }\n        }\n        PosixFiles.makePrivate(file, \"audit log\");\n        if (requirePrivate) {\n            // Redundant with the chmod above on a normal filesystem, and the point is to notice the\n            // case where it is not: an inherited default ACL can widen what we just set.\n            PosixFiles.assertNoGroupOrOtherAccess(file, \"audit log\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Appends one event. The only identifier accepted is an {@link Identity}, which cannot print\n     * its value; anything else about the event comes from the {@link Reason} enum or a bounded long.\n     */\n    synchronized void append(Reason reason, Identity subject) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        StringBuilder line = new StringBuilder(96);\n        line.append(\"ts=\").append(TimeSource.system().nowEpochSeconds())\n            .append(\" event=\").append(reason.name())\n            .append(\" msg=\\\"\").append(scrub(reason.genericUserMessage())).append('\"');\n        if (subject != null) {\n            line.append(\" subject=\").append(subject); // Identity.toString() is kind[len=N]\n        }\n        writeLine(line.toString());\n    }\n\n    /** Operational event with no subject. The kind is a closed enum, never free text. */\n    synchronized void appendEvent(AuditEvent event) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        writeLine(\"ts=\" + TimeSource.system().nowEpochSeconds() + \" event=\" + event.describe());\n    }\n\n    private void writeLine(String candidate) throws IdentityStoreException {\n        String line = scrub(candidate) + System.lineSeparator();\n        byte[] bytes = line.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);\n        try {\n            long current = Files.exists(file, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS) ? Files.size(file) : 0L;\n            if (current + bytes.length > maxBytes) {\n                if (!warnedAboutCap) {\n                    warnedAboutCap = true;\n                    // stderr, not the log: the log is the thing that is full.\n                    System.err.println(\"audit log reached its configured size limit; further events\"\n                            + \" are not being recorded\");\n                }\n                throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.AUDIT_FAILURE,\n                        \"the audit log has reached its configured size limit\");\n            }\n        } catch (IOException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.AUDIT_FAILURE, \"cannot size the audit log\", e);\n        }\n        try {\n            // CREATE here is load-bearing: a deleted log must be recreated, or one `rm` becomes a\n            // permanent outage. NOFOLLOW_LINKS is enforced by the platform, not by convention -\n            // verified on this JDK: an append through a symlink at the target throws instead of\n            // writing through it, so the path cannot be redirected at another file.\n            Files.write(file, bytes, StandardOpenOption.WRITE, StandardOpenOption.APPEND,\n                    StandardOpenOption.CREATE, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS);\n        } catch (IOException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.AUDIT_FAILURE, \"cannot append to the audit log\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    synchronized int lineCount() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try {\n            if (!Files.isRegularFile(file, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {\n                return 0;\n            }\n            try (java.util.stream.Stream<String> lines = Files.lines(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {\n                return (int) lines.count();\n            }\n        } catch (IOException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.AUDIT_FAILURE, \"cannot read the audit log\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /** For tests that must assert on log contents. */\n    synchronized String readAll() throws IdentityStoreException {\n        try {\n            if (!Files.isRegularFile(file, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {\n                return \"\";\n            }\n            return new String(Files.readAllBytes(file), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);\n        } catch (IOException e) {\n            throw new IdentityStoreException(Reason.AUDIT_FAILURE, \"cannot read the audit log\", e);\n        }\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void close() {\n        // Nothing to release: each append opens and closes, so no handle holds the file open\n        // between operations and the size cap cannot be evaded through a buffered writer.\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ scrubbing\n\n    private static final Pattern KEY_VALUE_SECRET = Pattern.compile(\n            // Key name may be preceded by _ or - (word boundaries would miss AUTH_DB_PASSWORD),\n            // and the value is taken to end-of-token *or* end-of-line so a quoted phrase with\n            // spaces is hidden in full rather than only up to the first space.\n            \"(?i)([\\\"'\\\\[\\\\s,;{(]|^)\"\n                    + There is no {@code of(String)}\n * that fabricates a token from caller-supplied structure; {@link #parse} accepts a submitted string\n * only as an opaque handle to look up, and only after checking its shape.\n *\n * <h2>What the database holds</h2>\n * Not this string. {@link #tokenHash()} is a SHA-256 digest, and the digest is the primary key of\n * the session row. A read of the {@code session} table - through a backup, a stolen file, or an\n * SQL-injection hole elsewhere in the product - therefore does not hand over live credentials:\n * the digest is not invertible and is what the server compares against. This is the same reason\n * a password database stores a hash rather than the password, applied to bearer tokens.\n *\n * <h2>Remaining risk, stated plainly</h2>\n * A bearer token is still a bearer token: whoever holds the 43 characters holds the session until\n * it expires or is revoked. Hashing protects the stored copy, not the copy in the caller's hand.\n * Mitigations in this code: short TTL (configuration-bounded at 24 h, default 15 min), absolute\n * per-account session cap, explicit revocation that also fires on a password change, and no\n * binding claim beyond the token itself - see README \"Limitations\" for what a real deployment adds\n * (TLS, per-Principal binding, and cookie attributes via {@link CookieSpec}).\n */\npublic record SessionToken(String value) {\n\n    static final int TOKEN_BYTES = 32;\n    static final int TOKEN_CHARS = 43; // ceil(32*8/6), base64url with the '=' padding removed\n    private static final Base64.Encoder B64URL = Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding();\n    private static final Base64.Decoder B64URL_DEC = Base64.getUrlDecoder();\n\n    public SessionToken {\n        // The canonical constructor is the choke point: a token that did not come from\n        // generate() must still be exactly the shape generate() produces.\n        if (value == null || value.length() != TOKEN_CHARS) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"session token must be \" + TOKEN_CHARS + \" characters\");\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; i < value.length(); i++) {\n            if (!isTokenChar(value.charAt(i))) {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"session token has a disallowed character\");\n            }\n        }\n        byte[] raw = decodeOrThrow(value);\n        if (raw.length != TOKEN_BYTES) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"session token does not decode to 32 bytes\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    /** Fresh token from the platform CSPRNG. */\n    public static SessionToken generate(SecureRandom random) {\n        byte[] raw = new byte[TOKEN_BYTES];\n        random.nextBytes(raw);\n        try {\n            return new SessionToken(B64URL.encodeToString(raw));\n        } finally {\n            java.util.Arrays.fill(raw, (byte) 0);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Validates a submitted token. would never write is refused, not repaired\");\n        Harness.Fixture f = Harness.fixture(\"corrupt-read\", Harness.overrides());\n        try (Harness.Bundle b = Harness.openApi(f)) {\n            Harness.register(b, Harness.E1, Harness.U1, Harness.P1);\n            Harness.register(b, Harness.E2, Harness.U2, Harness.P2);\n\n            check(\"both accounts authenticate before we start An email column that is no longer an address. The username still matches, so the\n            //    row is still reachable - only re-validation stands between it and an outcome.\n            Harness.rawExecute(f, \"UPDATE account SET email_canon = 'not an address'\"\n                    + \" WHERE username_canon = 'alice'\");\n            AuthResult viaBadEmail = b.api.signIn(Harness.U1, Harness.chars(Harness.P1), SourceId.LOCAL);\n            check(\"a row whose email fails validation cannot be authenticated into\",\n                    !viaBadEmail.isSuccess());\n            check(\"and the refusal is the generic one\",\n                    viaBadEmail.userMessage().equals(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL.genericUserMessage()));\n            check(\"no session was issued\", viaBadEmail.token() == null);\n            check(\"the API surfaces it as a refusal rather than an exception\",\n                    viaBadEmail.reason() == Reason.BAD_CREDENTIAL);\n            check(\"the broken row was not silently normalised back into shape\",\n                    Harness.rawColumn(f, \"SELECT email_canon FROM account WHERE username_canon = 'alice'\")\n                            .equals(List.of(\"not an address\")));\n            check(\"the store itself reports the row corrupt (the detail the caller never sees)\",\n                    storeReportsCorrupt(b));\n\n            // 2.
